clue.text: One of two lines in hand-me-downs

definitions.text: One of two lines in hand-me-downs

parts.words: One of two lines in hand-me-downs
parts.note: the word hand-me-downs is written with two short joining dashes, and the clue asks for the name of either one

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a stitched seam or a pair of rows in second-hand clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests seams or stitching in old clothes; it means the little dashes printed in the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The short dash joining parts of a compound word is the punctuation sign the clue describes, and hand-me-downs contains two of them.

clue.text: Shetland island valley, last of it pointing north

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointing north means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards
only the last part of the word valley is used, its first two letters being dropped

explanation.surface: A travel note about a glen on a Scottish island facing the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of it' keeps LLEY from VALLEY, and 'pointing north' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the northern isles in the Shetland group off Scotland, so it is an example of the island named.

clue.text: One of the prelims that fill roughly middle of sheet

indicators.note: roughly signals that the letters of the words before it are only loosely arranged and must be reordered
the centre letter of the word sheet is taken

explanation.surface: A printer explains that some pages fill up about half a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges THAT FILL into HALFTITL, then the E from the centre of 'sheet' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The prelims are the front pages of a book before the main text, and this short-title page is one of them.

clue.text: New number underground

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs: the old anaesthetic gas ether

explanation.surface: A new figure turns up in the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that makes you numb, the anaesthetic ether.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or beneath, as in the nether regions, so it can stand for what lies below ground.

clue.text: Experts like lyrics based on foot beats

parts.note: experts are pros, short for professionals
odic means like an ode, a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Professionals say songs with good words grow out of tapping feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the metrical unit of verse, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosody is the study of metre, which is built on metrical feet and their stressed and unstressed beats.

clue.text: Amtrak put nuncio off reading aid

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy's train journey is cancelled, so he needs something to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges all fifteen letters of AMTRAK PUT NUNCIO. Amtrak is the US passenger railway; a nuncio is a papal ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Commas, stops and the like help a reader follow the sense of written text, so each sign is a reading aid.

clue.text: Smack forward child he'd brought in

parts.note: on means forward, as in moving on

indicators.note: brought in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: a tot is a small child
he'd taken without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cheeky child is smacked by a man who brought him indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' is the adverb, as in 'smack on time', not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: Smack, used as an adverb, means exactly or precisely, which is the idiom for being punctual to the second.

clue.text: Engineer has to take these in courts

definitions.text: Engineer has to take these in courts

indicators.note: engineer as a verb means contrive or rework, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer giving evidence must be sworn in before testifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person but is the instruction to rearrange HAS TO; the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Witnesses in court swear solemn promises to tell the truth before giving evidence, and these sworn vows are what the clue describes.

clue.text: One large boy struggled to limit onset of spotty rash

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: vied means competed or struggled

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A big boy fought to keep a spotty skin outbreak under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like the skin condition but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is hasty and unwise, so the adjective is a synonym for a poorly judged act.

clue.text: Terence wrote in this former city container

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
LA is Los Angeles
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Someone called Terence used to write from an old city in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence is the Roman comic playwright of the 2nd century BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dramatist Terence wrote his comedies in the early classical form of the Roman language, the tongue he used.

clue.text: Jot first of thoughts in book

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a title is a book, as publishers speak of new titles

indicators.note: the first letter of the word thoughts is used

explanation.surface: An instruction to note down your opening ideas in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jot' looks like a verb, write down, but is the noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A jot is a tiny amount, and the old phrase 'not one jot or one tittle' pairs the two as synonyms for a small dot.

clue.text: Article theorised about what lies beyond

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A paper speculating on the afterlife or the unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but rearranges THEORISED.
explanation.definitionFit: The far side of something, or the afterlife, is the place over the boundary, the region past where we are now.

clue.text: Noticed old American over here in Paris getting lucky

indicators.note: over means covering, so the first word wraps round the French word

parts.note: felt means sensed or noticed
ici is French for here
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: An old American notices people in Paris enjoy good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here in Paris' asks for the French word for here.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicitous means happily chosen or fortunate, so a felicitous outcome is a lucky one.

clue.text: Book former opening times

indicators.note: opening means cutting open, so the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so times gives two of them
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Reserve the old opening hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb, reserve; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A set work or textbook studied in a course is called a text, so the word can mean a book.

clue.text: Dismiss one in a cricket club, subject to hearing

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the club

parts.note: oust means throw out or dismiss
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cricket club sacks a player, who now faces a disciplinary hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' is not a tribunal but the sense of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic means relating to sound and the sense that detects it, so it covers the topic of hearing.

clue.text: Southern Dutch explorer keeps note for politician

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Dutch explorer in the south carries a letter for a minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a musical note, te from do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced, respected political leader is called by this word, so it suits a politician.

clue.text: Munro carries round UV lamp primarily for Greek dish

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so these pieces go inside the writer's pen name

parts.note: H. H. Munro wrote short stories under the pen name Saki
a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word lamp is used

explanation.surface: Someone called Munro brings an ultraviolet lamp mainly for cooking Greek food.
explanation.walkthrough: Munro is not a Scottish mountain here but the Edwardian short-story writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvlaki are skewers of grilled meat, a familiar dish of Greek cooking.

clue.text: Consul once reversed in for tour guides

parts.note: Cicero was a Roman consul in 63 BC

indicators.note: reversed means the short word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: A former consul switches to working as sightseeing escorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is Italian; guides were named after Cicero for their eloquence.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows visitors around sights, so the plural means sightseeing guides.

clue.text: Mean to conceal age and state

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide away, so these letters drop out of sight

parts.note: the mean is the average

explanation.surface: Someone means to hide how old they are and declare something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend; it is the noun for average.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly, so it is a synonym of state as a verb.

clue.text: Sign covering letter for foreign president

definitions.meaning: a bar written above a vowel to show it is long

explanation.surface: A president abroad signs a cover letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering letter' looks like a job-application letter but means a mark placed above a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the horizontal bar over a long vowel and the surname of the French head of state.

clue.text: I'd backed commercial vehicle into dais, creating obstacle

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the letters of I'd are read backwards
into means these pieces go inside the platform

parts.note: a dais is a raised stage
an ad is a commercial
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone reversed a commercial van onto a platform, causing a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' hints at reversing the van; it turns I'D into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap or something that holds you back is a hindrance, so it works as an obstacle.

clue.text: Serious reduction in hospital department

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the department

parts.note: A and E is the UK hospital accident and emergency department
a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: A serious cutback in an emergency ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E is the British name for the emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute illness or crisis is severe and pressing, so the adjective can mean serious.

clue.text: Ammunition's more than adequate for platoon

indicators.note: the long word is more than enough to supply the short one, which sits within it

explanation.surface: A quartermaster confirms there are plenty of bullets for the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ammunition's more than adequate for' says the long word holds more than the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of a company of soldiers, a military unit.

clue.text: Link 100 popular clearing banks

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: clearing the banks means removing the outer letters, the edges of the word

explanation.surface: A hundred popular high-street banks merge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing banks' are high-street banks, but here it means strip the edges off 'popular'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a copula is a linking verb such as 'be' that joins subject and complement, so it is a link.

clue.text: This writer's probing a familiar resentment

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the first piece goes inside

parts.note: a crony is a close companion, a familiar
the setter refers to themself: this writer is = I am, shortened

explanation.surface: A columnist digs into an old friend's bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'familiar' is a noun, an intimate friend, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitterness or ill feeling, so it is a synonym of resentment.

clue.text: Choirmaster is keen to accommodate minor star

indicators.note: to accommodate means to hold inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A choir director gladly makes room for a junior soloist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor star' looks like a lesser celebrity; it is a little star-shaped symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol is named from Greek for little star, so it is literally a small star.

clue.text: Number seven in Etymology section

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from the words, here a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry refers to item seven in the word-origins part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seven' pretends to be the number; the letters run across 'seven in Etymology'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a whole number, ten times nine, so it is an example of a number.
